claims.statement: The object model is exactly nine @Entity classes in com.caozhihu.tmall.pojo — Category, Property, Product, PropertyValue, ProductImage, Review, User, Order and OrderItem — discovered through the SessionFactory's packagesToScan = com.caozhihu.*; the annotations are the only mapping metadata (no .hbm.xml) and hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=none means no DDL or schema validation at startup, so src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql is the sole definition of tables and columns and a renamed field surfaces as an SQL error on first use.

Every entity uses the same identity strategy: a primitive int id annotated @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) with @Column(name = "id") (Product's @Column is bare and falls back to id), matching the script's id int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT.

Because identity generation executes the INSERT during save(), the generated key is readable immediately afterwards — CategoryAction.add names the uploaded image file from category.getId() and ForeAction.buyone returns the new OrderItem id — while BaseServiceImpl.save's cast of the returned key to Integer means changing an entity's @Id to long breaks every insert on that service with a ClassCastException.

Table names are the class name lowercased except where annotated: category, property, product, propertyvalue, productImage, review, user, orderItem and order_ — Order maps to order_ to avoid the reserved word — and the annotated productImage/orderItem differ only in case from the script's productimage/orderitem, which resolves to the same table because neither side quotes identifiers.

All eleven relationships are unidirectional @ManyToOne with an explicit @JoinColumn declared on the many side: Product.category and Property.category over cid; ProductImage.product over pid; PropertyValue.product/property over pid/ptid; Review.user/product over uid/pid; Order.user over uid; OrderItem.product/order/user over pid/oid/uid. No entity maps @OneToMany, @ManyToMany or mappedBy, so no association has an inverse side.

Because a parent cannot hand out its children, every parent-scoped list is a query from the child's service, and the generic helpers BaseServiceImpl.listByParent, list(Page, parent) and total(parent) derive the criteria property from the uncapitalized simple name of the parent's class (Category -> "category", Order -> "order", Product -> "product"), making the child's Java field name a cross-class contract with no compile-time check.

The pair-parameter helper BaseServiceImpl.list(Object... pairParams) folds key/value pairs into a map and emits Restrictions.isNull(key) for a null value and Restrictions.eq(key, value) otherwise; that is how order-less cart lines are found (orderItemService.list("user", user, "order", null)), and because the pairs go into a map a repeated key silently discards the earlier pair.

Because User maps no orders collection, "my orders" is a criteria query rather than an association traversal: OrderServiceImpl.listByUserWithoutDelete builds eq("user", user) plus ne("status", OrderService.delete) over the Order class.

Every list helper appends Order.desc("id"), so values the UI calls "first" are the highest-id row: ProductImageServiceImpl.setFirstProductImage takes element 0 of list("product", product, "type", type_single), i.e. the newest single-type image, and returns early when the field is already set, which makes it idempotent across ProductServiceImpl.fill and OrderItemServiceImpl.fill.

ProductImage stores no image bytes: the row holds only product (pid) and type, while the JPEG lives on disk as <id>.jpg under img/productSingle or img/productDetail, a folder ProductImageAction.add chooses from type and where single images also get resized copies; any type that is not exactly type_single (including null) is treated as a detail image, and the type vocabulary (type_single/type_detail) is declared on ProductImageService and duplicated as a literal in the admin JSP.

PropertyValue is the only entity with two parent associations — Product over pid and Property over ptid, plus a free-text value column — and the script constrains only ptid with a foreign key; rows are created lazily by PropertyValueServiceImpl.init(Product), which walks the category's properties and inserts a blank value row for each missing (product, property) pair, and PropertyValueAction.edit calls init(product) before listByParent(product) because nothing else creates those rows.

No code path deletes a PropertyValue pair, so removing a Property leaves its values behind — the gap PropertyAction.delete's own comment admits when it asks what should happen to the property values of a deleted category property.

Review references a User (uid) and a Product (pid) but carries no order or order-item reference, so no row records which purchase produced it and nothing enforces one review per user or per order; content is varchar(4000) and the single write path is ReviewServiceImpl.saveReviewAndUpdateOrderStatus, which updates the order status and inserts the review in one transaction.

User maps only id, password and name; the password is compared in clear text through an equality criterion in UserServiceImpl.get(name, password) with no hashing or salting, name has no uniqueness constraint in the entity or the DDL (only the application-level UserService.isExit pre-check), and the name is HTML-escaped at registration and login.

OrderItem is both the cart line and the order line, distinguished by whether oid is set: cart lines carry uid with oid null, and OrderServiceImpl.createOrder saves the Order, then sets oi.setOrder(order) on each line and updates it in one transaction; the script leaves oid without a foreign key even though the association is mapped.

Money for an order is never stored on the order or item rows: number is the only varied quantity and every total is recomputed as number x product.promotePrice, so an order's total changes when the product's price changes afterwards.

promotePrice is the price used for money (cart total, Order.total recomputation, order creation) while originalPrice is read only by JSPs as a comparison price, and stock is display-and-script data: the only writer of setStock under src/ is Struts parameter binding from the admin product forms, no purchase path reads or decrements it, and the cart's "cannot exceed stock" rule is client-side JavaScript while ForeAction.buyone/addCart add num items without a stock check.

Ten @Transient fields exist across three entities — Category.products and Category.productsByRow; Product.firstProductImage, productSingleImages, productDetailImages, reviewCount and saleCount; Order.orderItems, total and totalNumber — and Hibernate never writes, reads back or allows them in criteria or HQL, so they are not queryable and are lost on a save/update round-trip.

ProductServiceImpl.fill(List) sets Category.products for each category and ProductServiceImpl.fillByRow(List) chunks that list into rows of 8 to set productsByRow; fillByRow reads category.getProducts() instead of querying, so it throws NullPointerException unless fill ran first, and ForeAction.home is the only caller that runs them in that order.

Product.firstProductImage is filled by ProductImageServiceImpl.setFirstProductImage and reached from ProductServiceImpl.fill, OrderItemServiceImpl.fill, ForeAction.product/forecategory-search paths, ProductAction.list and the cart screens; the admin image screens instead populate Action4Pojo.productSingleImages/productDetailImages, so Product.productSingleImages/productDetailImages are populated only on the storefront product path.

ProductServiceImpl.setSaleAndReviewNumber sets Product.saleCount by summing OrderItem.number over all order items of the product with no order-status filter, so lines still sitting in a cart (oid null) are counted as sold, and sets Product.reviewCount from reviewService.total(product), a plain count(*) over Review for the product.

Order.orderItems, Order.total and Order.totalNumber are filled only at read time by OrderItemServiceImpl.fill(Order)/(List) — orderItems from listByParent(order), total as the sum of number x product.promotePrice and totalNumber as the sum of number — and this transient total is distinct from the value OrderService.createOrder returns (which ForeAction.createOrder stores in the action's own float total field, Action4Parameter.total).

Order.getStatusDesc() switches on the status string and maps the six OrderService constants to 待付/待发/待收/等评/完成/刪除, keeping the initialised "未知" for unrecognised values; the vocabulary itself is declared as string constants on the OrderService interface (not on the entity), the only reader of statusDesc is web/admin/listOrder.jsp, and because the switch switches on status itself a null status throws NullPointerException at render time even though the DDL column is nullable and only the write paths (createOrder, payed, OrderAction.delivery, orderConfirmed, doreview, deleteOrder) guarantee a value.

User.getAnonymousName() derives a masked display name that is never persisted — null name returns null, length <= 1 returns "*", length 2 returns the first character plus "*", and longer names keep the first and last character with every character between them replaced by "*" — and the JSPs rendering reviews are its only consumers.

The OrderService status values and ProductImageService type values are the app's string vocabularies and live on service interfaces rather than entities, so an entity has no compile-time knowledge of the values it may hold and a changed constant string silently breaks the literals already stored by the seed script and the duplicated literals in JSPs such as the hidden productImage.type input and the storefront's ${o.status=='waitPay'} comparisons.

Deleting a parent row is limited by the hand-written DDL rather than by the mapping, because no association declares cascade and each delete action issues a single delete on one row: nine of the eleven join columns carry a foreign key (product.cid, property.cid, productimage.pid, propertyvalue.ptid, order_.uid, review.uid, review.pid, orderitem.uid, orderitem.pid) so the database rejects deleting a parent that still has children, while propertyvalue.pid and orderitem.oid have no constraint and let child rows survive as orphans.

Because every association is a default (EAGER) @ManyToOne, loading an OrderItem also loads its Product, Order and User and loading a Product loads its Category, which is what lets JSPs navigate oi.product.promotePrice on objects that are already detached — the application installs no OpenSessionInView filter (web.xml declares only the struts2 and encodingFilter filters), so a future @OneToMany or fetch = LAZY would move the failure to render time.

Adding an entity requires a matching service implementation, because BaseServiceImpl resolves its own entity class by reflection from the subclass name (...ServiceImpl in ...service.impl rewritten to ...pojo), so an entity without its ServiceImpl twin leaves clazz null and fails on the first query — the naming convention is a load-bearing extension boundary of the domain model.

README.md's relationship table disagrees with the annotations in one row — its last entry reads User-用户 / User-评价, naming User again on the many side, whereas the real association is Review.user over review.uid — and it also describes the stack as MySQL while the checked-in runtime runs H2 in MySQL mode against the adapted script, and says nothing about the @Transient fields or the derived accessors the storefront depends on.
